newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Bruton firm on EU timetable for treaty rewrite.
newsitem.headline: Bruton firm on EU timetable for treaty rewrite.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton on Saturday played down talk that the European Union might have to hold another series of treaty negotiations if the current round failed or did not achieve enough.

Speaking before hosting a special EU summit to discuss the bloc's future, Bruton said that it would be more difficult later to agree tough decisions because of the EU's plans to expand into eastern Europe and the Mediterranean.
"There is a strong practical reason for doing as much work as we possibly can and hopefully all of the work in this treaty and not leaving anything over," he told reporters.

"I think it is very important that we do as much as we can now because we have to bear in mind that we've agreed (to) commence the enlargement negotiations six months after (this) treaty is put in place."
The EU is negotiating changes to its treaty so that it can work efficiently when it brings in more members.

"Now if it's difficult to get agreement among 15 heads of government on a treaty to deal with very difficult and major problems, obviously if we try to do it later on, when we have enlarged and are more than 20 members, it will be even more difficult," he said.

On a visit to Dublin earlier in the week, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl suggested that EU's Maastricht treaty might have to be revised a second time -- after the current negotiations -- because of difficulties between member states.
But Bruton said that a new treaty should not be put into cold storage because of British elections due by next May and Prime Minister John Major's domestic problems with so-called Eurosceptics.
"I don't think any general election in any country has an overwhelming effect on the issue," he said.
